results.title: Lee approves confirmation hearing requests for justice minister, tax agency chief nominees
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung has approved requests for parliamentary confirmation hearings for Justice Minister nominee Lee Yong-cheol and Ahn Duk-su, his pick to head the National Tax Service (NTS), the presidential office said Monday. Lee nominated the two officials on Nov. 6. Their confirmation hearings are expected to focus on their qualifications and policy positions on key government issues, including prosecution reform and tax administration. Lee Yong-cheol worked on prosecution reform while serving as senior presidential secretary for civil affairs and legal affairs under former President Roh Moo-hyun, who served from 2003 to 2008. Lee also served on the transition team after Lee Jae Myung was elected mayor of Seongnam, south of Seoul, in June 2010. results.title: Nat'l baseball team manager apologizes for losses vs. Japan at regional tournament
results.content: The national baseball team manager Choi Won-ho apologized to fans Monday as Korea's losses against Japan piled up at a regional tournament in Tokyo. Choi and his team returned home Monday after finishing in second place behind Japan at the third edition of the Asia Professional Baseball Championship (APBC), an under-24 competition that also featured Taiwan and Australia. This was Korea's third straight runner-up finish in this competition, following 2017 and 2023. Choi's team lost to Australia 8-7 to begin round-robin action Thursday and then dropped to Japan 9-5 the next day. Korea defeated Taiwan 6-4 on Saturday to book a spot in the final and a rematch against the undefeated Japan. Korea managed just five hits in a 5-1 loss in Sunday's final at Tokyo Dome, and Korea's losing skid against Japan in games featuring professionals reached 13. results.title: North Jeolla to mount solo bid for 2036 Summer Olympics after talks with Seoul fall through
results.content: North Jeolla Province announced Monday it will mount a solo bid for the 2036 Summer Olympics after talks with Seoul over potential co-hosting fell through. In a statement, the province said its governor, Lee Won-taeg, and Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon met last Thursday and decided against a joint bid "out of respect for realistic conditions and positions for both sides," without elaborating further. "We will now make a concerted push to host the Olympics alone," the province added. In February 2025, North Jeolla beat out Seoul to become Korea's sole candidate for the 2036 Olympics. The province later shifted toward co-hosting the event with the capital city, after concluding that it did not have adequate infrastructure, covering accommodations, transportation and venues, to host the competition alone. results.title: Call of Duty enlists JAMBINAI to give its score a Korean touch
results.content: When it came to making the score for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, the composers wanted to find something special to emphasize the Korean settings in parts of the video game. The military first-person shooter, which has received global attention after being released by Activision on Oct. 23, centers on a military conflict that begins on the Korean Peninsula. Jonathan Mayer, founder of video game music production company Spider Farm Productions, invited the Korean band JAMBINAI to work with composers Stephen Barton and Jason Graves. "We wanted to include a lot of the traditional sounds of Korean music but in ways that felt woven into the fabric of the music rather than sprinkled on top," Mayer said. results.title: Thailand seeks swift conclusion to CEPA talks with Korea
results.content: MANILA — Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul called for an early trade deal with Korea to unlock the two countries’ growth potential during a bilateral summit with President Lee Jae Myung in the Philippines, Monday. The meeting took place in Manila on the sidelines of the summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), an 11-member regional bloc, and related gatherings. “Thailand hopes to conclude the CEPA negotiations as soon as possible,” Anutin said, referring to a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement under negotiation between the two countries. The proposed bilateral pact covers goods, services and investment, alongside broader economic cooperation. Korea and Thailand announced the launch of negotiations in March 2024 and held their first formal round in July that year. results.title: Lee pledges to expand AI, cultural cooperation with ASEAN
results.content: MANILA — President Lee Jae Myung pledged to expand cooperation with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), an 11-member regional bloc, on artificial intelligence (AI) and cultural industries during the annual Korea-ASEAN summit in the Philippines, Monday. “Korea will take the lead in ensuring that everyone benefits from advances in AI technology and that the cultural creativity of ASEAN’s young people leads to new opportunities,” Lee said in his keynote speech at the Philippine International Convention Center in Manila. The president proposed the two areas of cooperation as the next steps in advancing his Korea-ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP) vision, saying the framework unveiled a year earlier is beginning to produce concrete results. results.title: Korean Series heroes hit KBO free agency
results.content: SEOUL, Nov. 16 (Yonhap) -- The reigning Korean Series MVP and another postseason hero for the Samsung Lions will be among 22 free agents in South Korean baseball this offseason. The Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) released the list of free agents on Monday, with 22 out of 26 eligible players choosing to exercise their rights. Koo Ja-wook, who captained the Lions to their first title since 2014 and was voted the Korean Series MVP, headlines the group. The 33-year-old outfielder is joined by the 26-year-old pitcher Won Tae-in, the winning pitcher in the clinching Game 5 of the Korean Series against the KT Wiz. Both players have only played for the Lions so far in their KBO careers -- Koo since 2015 and Won since 2019. results.title: N. Korean nuclear issue unlikely to feature prominently at Trump-Xi-Putin summit: experts
results.content: MANILA — North Korea's nuclear weapons program is unlikely to feature prominently at an unprecedented summit among the leaders of the United States, China and Russia set to be held this week, though the gathering could provide a limited opening for renewed diplomatic contact between Washington and Pyongyang, U.S. experts said Monday. U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are scheduled to hold their first-ever trilateral summit Thursday in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, where nuclear arms reduction is expected to be discussed. Although Trump has previously expressed interest in meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong-un again, a U.S. administration official said last week that there are no plans for engagement with Pyongyang during the president's Asia trip. results.title: 'Don't say we've grown distant': BTS' V explains year-end awards absence
results.content: BTS member V has reassured fans that the group's absence from Korea's year-end music awards ceremonies does not mean the global superstars have grown distant from their roots or their supporters. "Please don't say we've become distant just because we're global stars," V said in a lengthy message posted Sunday on the fan platform Weverse, addressing disappointment among fans hoping to see BTS perform at year-end award shows. The singer added a playful remark to emphasize that the members have not changed despite their international fame. "We can still take pictures of ourselves picking our noses," he said. His comments came after BTS won six awards at the 2026 Melon Music Awards (MMA), held Saturday and Sunday at Gocheok Sky Dome in Seoul, including two grand prizes — Album of the Year and Artist of the Year. results.title: Seoul stocks dip over 3% on tech losses amid lingering Nvidia jitters
results.content: South Korean stocks sank by more than 3 percent Monday as foreign investors sold tech shares amid lingering artificial intelligence (AI) boom concerns following the fallout at Nvidia. The Korean won strengthened against the US dollar. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) lost 190.03 points, or 3.59 percent, to close at 5,100.5, extending its losses to a third session. The decline extended Friday's losses amid uncertainty over the outlook for the global AI industry following the ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, a key figure in driving the global AI boom. Investor sentiment remained cautious ahead of Nvidia's earnings report and Anthropic's anticipated Nasdaq debut later this week, amid concerns that the high-profile listing could divert investment from other technology stocks. results.title: 'Like novels and films, games also hinge on the story they tell'
results.content: "Can artificial intelligence (AI) provide answers to the problems of human society? We ourselves cannot even answer the fundamental question of what it means to be human," said novelist Lee Woo-hyuk at a discussion hosted by Game Generation, a cultural criticism webzine run by the Game Culture Foundation, at PUBG Seongsu in Seongdong District, Seoul, on Friday. Veteran creators who have spent decades grappling with storytelling expressed little belief that AI could replace human creativity in narrative writing. At the event, Lee — best known for his series "Toemarok" — said AI might be capable of producing rudimentary stories, but narratives that grapple with deeper questions ultimately require a human touch. results.title: AI movie 'Raphael' impresses visually, lacks fresh plot
results.content: As artificial intelligence (AI) continues to reshape the filmmaking landscape, the upcoming sci-fi drama "Raphael" pushes the technology to its limits as Korea's first feature-length film created entirely with generative AI. Set to hit local theaters on Nov. 25, the movie stands out for its polished visuals and ambitious philosophical questions, even if its narrative relies heavily on familiar genre formulas. Co-directed by Yang Ik-june, Moon Shin-woo and Jung Joo-won, and produced by Matteo AI Studio alongside MBC C&I AI Contents Lab, "Raphael" was completed over 14 months without shooting a single scene with real actors. Aside from initial planning and screenwriting, generative AI was used to build every element of the film, from character appearances and ruined future landscapes to voice acting, music and sound effects. results.title: Korea seeks to reconstruct aging embassy in US amid uncertainty over funding
results.content: The foreign ministry said Monday that it has been seeking to reconstruct its aging embassy building in Washington in a project estimated to cost 264.6 billion won ($198 million), but its funding request has not yet been included in next year's government budget proposal. The ministry made the request to rebuild the building, which was erected in 1954, in 2023, last year and this year due to safety issues, limits to performing diplomatic activities in the aging facilities and concerns about the impact on the national image, it said. The budget subcommittee of the National Assembly's finance, economy, planning and budget committee did not discuss the embassy reconstruction issue in a recent budget deliberation session, an official at the legislature's foreign affairs committee said, a sign that the project could again fail to move forward this year. results.title: Korea courts global space partnerships as private sector takes lead
results.content: Korea's space industry seeks to turn its growing technological capabilities into international business opportunities as government officials and industry representatives from 18 countries gather in Seoul for a forum focused on commercial space cooperation. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Korea AeroSpace Administration jointly hosted the second Global New Space Forum at the Four Seasons Hotel Seoul on Monday, bringing together representatives of about 40 Korean companies and government officials from 18 countries and international organizations. The gathering aims to connect Korean space companies with overseas agencies and identify opportunities for joint research, technology demonstrations and commercial partnerships. results.title: S. Korea's chief nuclear envoy calls for humanitarian cooperation with N. Korea in 'feasible' areas
results.content: South Korea should seek humanitarian cooperation with North Korea in healthcare, disaster response and other "feasible" areas to make progress in improving human rights, and contribute to peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula, Seoul's top nuclear envoy said Monday. Jeong Yeon-doo, vice foreign minister for diplomatic strategy and intelligence, made the remarks in opening remarks at a forum on human rights in North Korea in Seoul. "Efforts to explore transparent and sustainable humanitarian cooperation, starting with such feasible areas as healthcare and disaster response, could contribute to tangible improvements in human rights in North Korea, and peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula," Jeong was quoted as saying by the ministry. results.title: KakaoBank launches Apple Pay, ending Hyundai Card's monopoly
results.content: KakaoBank has launched Apple Pay in Korea, Monday, ending Hyundai Card's run as the only local financial institution offering the mobile payment service. The internet-only lender said customers can now add their debit cards to Apple Wallet and use them to make payments through Apple Pay. Users can make payments at participating offline stores, including major retailers, pharmacies, restaurants, cafes and convenience stores. To pay, they can simply double-click the side button on an iPhone or Apple Watch, authenticate the transaction using Face ID, Touch ID or a device passcode, and hold the device near a payment terminal. Apple Pay is also available for online and in-app purchases on iPhones, iPads and Macs, allowing users to check out without repeatedly entering their card numbers or delivery information. results.title: AI cheating is forcing Korea to rethink CSAT
results.content: Ten seconds. That was all it took for artificial intelligence (AI) glasses to solve four college entrance exam-style math questions in a recent demonstration by The Korea Times. For Korea’s make-or-break annual College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), the immediate question is how to keep that kind of assistance out of the exam room. The larger one is whether keeping AI out would resolve a more fundamental issue: what students should be learning in an AI-driven world. In the short term, finding solutions to the first question is crucial to keeping the exam fair and credible. The recent tax-accountant examination cheating case shows that one can use AI with a miniature camera and smartphone to obtain answers throughout an exam without being detected. results.title: Court rules Korea Zinc management misused company assets to block MBK-Young Poong voting rights
results.content: A Seoul court has overturned key resolutions passed at Korea Zinc’s annual shareholders’ meeting last year, ruling that the company’s incumbent management improperly used corporate assets to block the voting rights of the MBK Partners-Young Poong alliance, its largest shareholder, industry officials said Monday. In its Nov. 12 ruling, the Seoul Central District Court described the actions as “the private use of company assets” and said they “clearly violated directors’ duty of loyalty,” according to the alliance. The ruling marks a new development in the protracted battle for control of the world’s largest refined zinc smelter between Chairman Choi Yun-beom’s camp and the MBK Partners-Young Poong alliance that has dragged on since 2024. results.title: Remains of fallen Korean War soldier returned to family after 75 years
results.content: The remains of a fallen Korean War soldier were returned to his family in a ceremony Monday, more than seven decades after he was killed in action during the 1950-53 conflict, the defense ministry said. The ceremony honoring late Pfc. Ahn Dong took place in the southwestern city of Iksan, about 180 kilometers south of Seoul, about two months after authorities confirmed his identity through DNA testing, the ministry said in a release. Ahn's remains were first discovered in 2004 in the northeastern county of Goseong during an excavation operation by the defense ministry's war dead recovery agency. Although the agency obtained DNA samples from his family in 2019, it was unable to confirm a match until September of this year due to technological limitations. results.title: Naver shares slide on weak earnings, Nvidia leadership uncertainty
results.content: Naver is facing a wave of brokerage price target cuts as disappointing third-quarter earnings and uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership transition put pressure on its shares, market analysts said Monday. With margins shrinking in its core platform business, investors are looking for evidence that the company’s substantial spending on artificial intelligence (AI) data centers can generate profits and support a stock recovery. Shinhan Securities cut its price target to 280,000 won ($210) from 310,000 won Monday, joining other brokerages in lowering their valuations. SK Securities previously reduced its target to 260,000 won from 320,000 won, while Meritz Securities lowered its target to 270,000 won from 330,000 won. results.title: Benchmark rate for banks' mortgage loans continues to rise
results.content: The benchmark rate for banks' mortgage rates increased for a second consecutive month in October in line with high market rates, data showed Monday. COFIX, or the Cost of Funds Index, a benchmark lending rate for new mortgage loans, came to 3.62 percent last month, up 0.19 percentage point from the previous month, according to the data from the Korea Federation of Banks. The rate was the highest since February 2024, when the corresponding reading was 3.62 percent. COFIX is calculated based on the funding costs of eight domestic banks in Korea. They include Nonghyup Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank and Citibank Korea. The Bank of Korea (BOK) kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged last month at 3 percent after two consecutive rate hikes to give the central bank time to assess economic conditions amid prolonged tensions in the Middle East and robust exports. results.title: S. Korea voices hope upcoming US-China-Russia summit will advance peace on Korean Peninsula
results.content: South Korea hopes the upcoming summit among the leaders of the United States, China and Russia will contribute to peace on the Korean Peninsula and that its position will be fully taken into account, the foreign ministry said Monday. US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold their first-ever trilateral summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, according to the White House and the Kremlin. White House spokesperson Olivia Wales has said Trump plans to discuss reducing nuclear weapons worldwide at the meeting, while experts said Korean Peninsula issues could also be discussed given the three countries' respective interests in the region. results.title: Banks court religious communities with tailored financial services
results.content: Korea's major banks are courting religious communities to expand their customer base, offering tailored services such as mobile donation platforms and debit cards that double as membership cards for religious groups, industry officials said Monday. Hana Bank's mobile donation service for religious organizations processed 68 billion won ($51 million) in donations from January through October this year, according to the bank. This is a sharp increase from the 350 million won recorded in 2020, when the service was first introduced. The service allows worshippers at churches and Buddhist temples to make donations using QR codes, without having to install a separate app. Religious organizations can also link transaction data to their financial management systems, making it easier to issue donation receipts for year-end tax deductions. results.title: Ex-deputy national security adviser takes office as KOICA chief
results.content: Oh Hyun-joo, a career diplomat who previously served as a deputy director at the presidential National Security Office, took office Monday as the 15th president of the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), the state-run foreign aid agency. KOICA is Korea’s main agency for carrying out the government’s grant aid programs for developing countries. It was founded in 1991. An inauguration ceremony was held the same day at its headquarters in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. Oh graduated from Korea University with a degree in Spanish language and literature and earned a master’s degree in international relations from the University of Cambridge. She joined the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in 1994 after passing the foreign service exam. results.title: Local Oxford imprint aims to bring more Korean stories to English readers
results.content: Korean literature is set to reach more English-speaking readers through a new publishing imprint established by Oxford University's Korean studies center. The Oxford Centre for Korean Studies (OCKS) said Monday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with a local independent publisher, Oxford eBooks, to establish K-PRESS — a new imprint dedicated to translating Korean literature into English, according to Yonhap News Agency. The first title to be published will be “Mother Star,” the English edition of actor and novelist Cha In-pyo's debut novel. Jieun Kiaer, director of the center, told Yonhap that barriers to translation and publication remain high, with English-language editions concentrated among a small number of Korean writers and genres. results.title: As DUI scandals rock Korean entertainment, Super Junior star's unusual decision resurfaces
results.content: As drunk driving scandals have repeatedly derailed celebrity careers in Korea and often forcing stars to suspend their activities or withdraw from the public eye, Super Junior member Kim Hee-chul's unusual decision to sell his car to eliminate the temptation to drive after drinking is drawing renewed attention following a recent incident involving actor Ko Kyung-pyo. Ko, known for his role in the hit Korean drama "Reply 1988," posted a lengthy apology on social media Sunday after crashing into a street-cleaning truck while driving under the influence (DUI) early Saturday. The collision left the truck's driver, a man in his 60s, injured. Ko's blood alcohol concentration reportedly exceeded Korea's legal threshold for driver's license revocation. results.title: HD Hyundai Heavy wins $203.6 mil. order for 4 LPG carriers
results.content: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries said Monday it has secured a 272.1 billion-won ($203.6 million) contract to build four liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) carriers. The South Korean shipbuilder said it will build the vessels for an undisclosed client in Oceania and deliver them by September 2029. The latest contract accounts for 1.55 percent of the company's annual sales, according to its regulatory filing.

results.title: Lee's Kosdaq reform push faces skepticism over lack of concrete measures
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung’s push to revive Kosdaq as part of broader capital market reforms is drawing skepticism, with market participants saying Monday that his proposals lack concrete measures to attract investment. They support removing weak companies and broadening the investor base but question whether the measures outlined so far will bring sustained capital inflows. At a policy meeting at the Korea Exchange on Friday, Lee acknowledged widespread concerns about Kosdaq and called for stricter enforcement of delisting rules to swiftly remove financially troubled or underperforming companies. The meeting followed steep declines in both KOSPI and Kosdaq from record highs earlier this year, fueling concerns about financial market stability. results.title: Seoul to transform hidden Sinchon hilltop into sunset, night-view park by 2027
results.content: A hidden hilltop park tucked just an eight-minute walk from Seoul’s bustling Sinchon university district is set to undergo a major transformation into a premier night tourism landmark by 2027. Seodaemun District said Monday that Changcheon Neighborhood Park, commonly known by locals as Baramsan (Wind Mountain) due to its breezy elevated terrain, has been selected for the Seoul Metropolitan Government's 2026 Seoul Starlight Attraction Creation Project. The district plans to invest up to 1 billion won in municipal funding following final budget reviews, supported by 50 million won in district funds already secured for initial master planning.
